subject: EU edge ingress disruption — temporary routing bridge & customer actions
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@retailco.com>
Cc: ops@acme-cloud.com
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: [INC-20290415-47] EU edge ingress disruption — immediate mitigation and routing bridge

Team / Sam —

Quick summary: between ~07:50–08:05 UTC we observed elevated packet loss on the EU edge peering path (eu-central-1) provided by our primary cloud partner. Symptoms: 5–12s tail latencies for handshake/initial token streams and intermittent request timeouts for sessions pinned to EU region. This resulted in higher request failures and some increased token costs as clients retried.

What we are doing now:
- Opened incident INC-20290415-47 and engaged partner NOC; root-cause investigation underway.
- Activated temporary routing bridge: we are shifting new connections from the impacted EU edge to our adjacent ingress POPs (US-west and APAC Singapore) for customers who opt-in. This is a network-level bypass — there is no model change.
- Published a short reroute checklist (attached) for customers that want to proactively point traffic to alternate ingress endpoints.

Immediate asks for customers:
1) If you can tolerate slightly higher RTT to a non-EU endpoint, switch to the regional endpoint below until we clear the peering issue:
   - api.redwood.com (global) -> prefer: api.us.redwood.com or api.apac.redwood.com
   - header option (no SDK change): X-Redwood-Region-Preference: us OR apac
2) For Dedicated customers: if your capacity is pinned to an EU-only pool and you want us to failover to reserved capacity in another region, reply with your pool id and authorization so we can coordinate (see note in checklist).
3) Confirm whether you want us to perform the IP-level reroute on your behalf (we can configure a customer-specific NAT bridge for short windows).

Temporary mitigations we recommend leaving in place until we close the incident: caching enabled (TTL 30s) on long prompt prefixes, client-side retry backoff to 2s base, and disable aggressive pinned session migration if you use sticky routing.

Attachments: reroute-checklist-20290415.csv (CSV with endpoints & step-by-step), small diagnostic snippet.

We will keep updates on the status page and follow up with a post-incident summary. I will also send an interim note when partner confirms peering restoration.

—David
David Kim
Senior Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

Sam —
Thanks for the quick reply. Short answers up front, details below.

- Dedicated EU pool impact: our Dedicated and Reserved GPU pools are not affected at the compute layer — jobs scheduled on pool-eu-7 continue to run. The observed problem is at the network/edge peering layer (ingress). That means requests that enter via the affected peering path may see failures; compute instances remain healthy.

- Re-auth: switching to api.us.redwood.com does not force immediate token rotation. Tokens are valid across our global control plane for the short-lived tokens you use. If you prefer a totally non-disruptive approach, we can establish a NAT bridge so your existing endpoints continue to resolve, and we proxy at the network edge to the US/APAC POPs. That approach preserves session cookies and avoids mass re-auth. It does introduce a short window for in-flight connection draining (we estimate <45s per connection).

- DNS/CN change window for our on-your-behalf reroute: if you authorize us, changes can be applied in ~10–15 minutes; full propagation and draining ~1–3 minutes of steady-state rebinds plus up to 45s for in-flight connections. We will coordinate maintenance window and provide a precise ETA once you approve.

Next steps I propose:
1) David — please add confirmed ETA for partner NOC and whether the peering fix includes route withdraw or hardware swap.
2) Sam — let me know if you authorize Redwood to perform the IP-level reroute for pool-eu-7 (reply with AUTH: REROUTE POOL-EU-7). I will schedule a short Zoom at 09:30 UTC to coordinate.
3) Monica — loop in Customer Success for credit/comp guidance if RetailCo requests a service credit.

Thanks — standing by to help with the switch.

—Neha Kapoor

Subject: [INC-20290415-47] Post-incident: findings, timeline, and next steps (EU edge)

Hi all —

Short post-incident summary and action items. Thank you for patience and cooperation — Sam, appreciate the quick coordination this morning.

Timeline (UTC):
- 07:48 — first packet-loss spike detected on eu-central-1 external uplink from partner (peering-eth2).
- 07:50 — system alerts, internal NOC paged; we create INC-20290415-47.
- 07:55 — Community routing fallback engaged, and Redwood initiated the temporary routing bridge for opt-in customers.
- 08:12 — David SRE posted initial customer guidance and checklist.
- 09:10 — RetailCo authorized REROUTE POOL-EU-7 (AUTH confirmed via account thread). Bridge applied; connections drained (~40s).
- 09:25 — Traffic stable on alternate POPs; no compute scheduling impacts observed on pool-eu-7.
- 11:40 — Partner NOC reports hardware replacement completed; peering path stable and packet loss returned to baseline at 11:36.
- 11:55 — Redwood began rolling traffic back to primary EU edge with controlled window; final verification at 12:05.

Root cause (high level):
Partner routing hardware (edge peering switch) experienced a faulty transceiver causing intermittent packet loss under moderate load. The partner replaced hardware at 11:40 UTC.

Customer impact summary:
- RetailCo (Dedicated pool-eu-7): minor short-lived request failures during 07:50–09:10 window while ingress was being switched; compute and scheduled jobs were unaffected.
- Non-dedicated / global customers: increased tail latency and elevated retry counts until reroute or peering fix.

Actions taken / mitigation we recommend (closures):
1) Short-term: maintain optional NAT bridge for customers that require zero re-auth; checklist attached.
2) Medium-term: we will add an additional health check and auto-failover rule at the edge to reduce detection-to-reroute time (target: <45s).
3) Long-term: beta of multi-homing peering logic (Q3 2029) to avoid single transceiver dependency per POP.

Credits / compensation: Monica, please coordinate RetailCo's request for credit. Based on our SLA matrix, this incident qualifies for a small prorated service credit; CS will reach out with the formal calculation.

Attachments included: incident-postmortem-20290415.pdf (detailed timeline + traceroutes), edge-logs-20290415.tar.gz (pcap & routing snapshots), reroute-checklist-20290415.csv.

If you need copies of any specific traces or a signed SLAsheet, reply and we will attach them. We will also publish the redacted postmortem to the customer portal tomorrow.

Thanks —
David Kim
Senior Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
